correctness.rationale: Sample all open edges first and restrict the same graph after each deletion. The burden counts ordered connected pairs, including diagonals, divided by the fixed original order for the expected outbreak. Benefit submodularity is therefore the nonnegative mixed difference of the unnormalized burden. Sites in separate components give zero. In the common component, after both sites are removed, every residual component touches at least one site. Writing A and B for the sizes attached only to one site and c_i for sizes attached to both, squares for singly attached pieces cancel. Expanding the remaining squares gives 2[(A+1)(B+1)−Σ_{i<j}c_i c_j]. With at most four vertices the sum is at most 1. Both statements hold pointwise. On a forest an ordered pair contributes its path-open probability times the indicator of deleting no vertex of the path; each indicator has nonnegative mixed difference, including the length-zero path. On C5, any nonempty deletion set leaves a forest. For adjacent sites at most one residual component in the open graph can touch both, so only nonadjacent sites at the empty set can give a negative difference. The two complementary routes for a pair at distance d=1 or 2 give connection probability p^d+p^(5−d)−p^5. Subtracting the two four-vertex path burdens and adding back the 3+2p residual burden gives 2p²(1+3p+5p²−10p³). The derivative of the cubic has a single positive zero, a maximum, and the cubic changes from +1 to −1 across [0,1], proving the unique threshold. Independent Boolean reachability enumeration gave no negative deterministic differences for n≤4 (1,586 cases for n=2–4), the exact C5 coefficient vector, and the gap −61009/160000 at p=19/20, giving −61009/800000 after normalization. Independent bisection gave 0.935152824805653192… . These checks establish the sharp onset without transferring it to other seeding conventions.
residual_risks: A source sampled only after deleting vertices changes the denominator; the homogeneous C5 threshold also does not assert a threshold for heterogeneous probabilities. The forest result and general deterministic identity rest on proof, not finite replay.

evidence: The closest indexed cycle theorem fixes an unvaccinated root, with cycle threshold p≤2/(n−1), a C4 failure and a rooted forest result.

Srivastava and Teng give general non-submodularity in network immunization and discuss complementarity of alternate paths. Li et al. prove submodularity for a single-source delayed-immunization tree model.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A fixed-root negative mixed difference need not survive averaging over sources, and root-deletion terms also matter when the source is allowed to be removed. Delayed immunization changes reachability. Neither result supplies the stated sharp uniform-seed cutoff.

evidence: The unique-path forest conclusion has standard rooted coverage content: extend each nonnegative survivor-root burden by zero on deletion of that root, and average; root-involving mixed differences are nonnegative by monotonicity. The averaged phase on C5 is different: the fixed-root threshold is 1/2 on C5, whereas the frozen one is approximately 0.93515.
General alternate-path complementarity does not specify its sign against fragmentation for every pair of sites, and the known fragmentation statistic does not supply the attachment formula.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the forest path mechanism and earlier evidence of non-submodularity. Neither implies the signed deterministic size identity, the universal sign cutoff, or the homogeneous C5 threshold; those are the supported distinct claims.

evidence: The exact unnormalized burden is |V−S| plus twice expected connected unordered survivor pairs; the modular first term and factor two do not affect the mixed-difference sign. One can also count disconnected pairs with the appropriate fixed-universe convention.
Chen et al. use a measure based on disconnected pairs after node removal; the inspected passage studies fragmentation under removal strategies rather than the mixed-difference criterion and C5 phase.

Pairwise fragmentation and fixed-root cycle comparisons
value.rationale: Expected pairwise connectivity is a standard measure of fragmentation, and diminishing returns is a meaningful structural property of the deletion benefit. The attachment formula identifies exactly what competes with fragmentation and explains why the first deterministic obstruction cannot arise below five vertices. The threshold gives both sides of the obstruction under iid edge thinning, rather than only an endpoint example at p=1. These are reusable mathematical facts even without an optimization theorem.
residual_risks: No transfer to real contact networks, time-dependent infection models, or vaccine strategy performance is claimed.
